reason: The inner disk’s rocky mixture should involve the disk’s hot inner orbits.
expectation: This will establish the hot inner region where rocky material is processed.

effect: The disk combined with the young Sun instead, establishing the hot inner region needed to process rocky material.
reaction: The automatic correction was useful; I had expected the inner orbits to work directly.
reason: Rock-forming dust seems like the natural material to process in the newly heated inner disk.

choice.combine: A disk with a hot inner region

expectation: The dust will be heated or separated into material for the inner disk’s rocky mixture.

effect: The hot inner region needed the inner orbits, producing vapor from evaporated grains; the rocky mixture will require further processing.
reaction: The correction clarified that inherited grains can be reprocessed by heat.
reason: Cooling the vapor seems like a plausible way to condense rocky solids.
expectation: The vapor will cool and form solid material for the inner disk.

effect: Cooling the vapor produced refractory mineral grains, a likely ingredient in the inner disk’s rocky mixture.
reaction: The condensation step made the heat-and-cooling sequence clear.
reason: The refractory grains and existing rock-forming dust seem like plausible components of the rocky mixture.
expectation: They will form a mixture of inner-disk rocky solids.

effect: The refractory grains and rock-forming dust formed a loose rocky aggregate, but the goal is not yet complete.
reaction: The mixture illustrates that grains can have different histories.
reason: Brief intense heating may further process the rocky aggregate into inner-disk material.
expectation: The aggregate will be heated into a more processed rocky component.

effect: Brief heating melted the aggregate into droplets; cooling them is the next plausible step toward rocky solids.
reaction: It is useful that the story leaves the disputed heating mechanism open.
reason: Radiation escaping into space previously cooled vapor, and may also cool the molten droplets.
expectation: The droplets will cool into solid rocky grains.

effect: The molten droplets cooled into chondrules, which may be a component of the inner disk’s rocky mixture.
reaction: The rounded particles preserve a useful record of their heating and cooling.
reason: Iron-bearing metal grains remain available and seem like a plausible addition to the rocky chondrules.
expectation: The chondrules and metal grains will form a rocky inner-disk mixture.

effect: The chondrules and metal formed the rocky mixture, completing the inner-disk goal; ice storage remains.
reaction: The distinction between mixed ingredients and a formed planet is helpful.
reason: Ice-mantled dust and cold outer orbits are the clearest available pieces for storing ice beyond the snow line.
expectation: The cold outer region will preserve the ice on the dust.

effect: The cold outer orbits preserved ice and dust, completing the remaining goal and the chapter.
reaction: The distinction between surviving inherited ice and vapor freezing again was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Cooling the molten droplets into chondrules was most worthwhile: their textures connect the combination to evidence of rapid heating and cooling.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first two guesses were less satisfying because both needed automatic compatibility corrections before the inner-disk sequence became clear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that inherited grains could evaporate and be thoroughly reprocessed in the hot inner disk, while inherited ice could survive farther out.

arbitrary.text: The initial requirement to combine the disk with the young Sun rather than directly with hot inner orbits was not obvious to me, although the result explained the heating.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the separate rocky and icy materials become larger bodies, especially with the same attention to what their ingredients reveal about their histories.
